label: Nature avoids the infinite and always seeks an end
claim: Nature avoids the infinite, because the infinite is unending and imperfect, and Nature always seeks an end; so spontaneously generated creatures cannot breed an endless series of new kinds.
quote: But Nature flies from the infinite, for the infinite is unending or imperfect, and Nature ever seeks an end.
scope: All of nature, applied here to the generation of animals
candidate_data: none known

label: Stationary testaceans and attached animals have no sexes
claim: Animals that do not move about, such as testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) and animals that live clinging to something, have no sexes, any more than plants do.
quote: But all those creatures which do not move, as the testacea and animals that live by clinging to something else, inasmuch as their nature resembles that of plants, have no sex any more than plants have
scope: Sessile animals: testaceans (bivalves, sea snails and the like) and attached animals (sponges, sea squirts, barnacles)
measurable_quantities: presence of separate sexes or hermaphroditism in sessile invertebrate taxa
candidate_data: Sexual-system and reproductive-mode annotations in the Animal Diversity Web and SeaLifeBase, with Open Tree of Life for taxon coverage.

label: The male supplies the efficient cause of generation, the female the material
claim: The male and female are the first principles of generation: the male supplies the efficient (moving) cause and the female supplies the material.
quote: the male and female principles may be put down first and foremost as origins of generation, the former as containing the efficient cause of generation, the latter the material of it.
scope: All animals with two sexes
candidate_data: none known

label: Castration changes nearly the whole form of a male toward the female
claim: When a male animal is castrated, although only the generative part is disabled, nearly its whole form changes so that it seems female or close to it.
quote: This is plain in the case of castrated animals, for, though only the generative part is disabled, yet pretty well the whole form of the animal changes in consequence so much that it seems to be female or not far short of it
scope: Castrated male animals (domestic livestock and men)
measurable_quantities: morphological traits (body shape, horn, voice, plumage, musculature) of castrated versus intact males and females
candidate_data: Livestock and veterinary studies comparing castrated, intact male and female animals; no single compiled database known.

label: Fishes and serpents have no testes, only two spermatic ducts
claim: Fishes and serpents have no testes at all, only two spermatic ducts.
quote: some of them have not testes at all, as the classes of fish and of serpents, but only two spermatic ducts.
scope: Fishes and snakes
measurable_quantities: presence of testes in male fishes and snakes
candidate_data: Comparative reproductive anatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; FishBase reproduction pages.

label: Birds and oviparous quadrupeds have internal testes near the loin
claim: All birds and all oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, tortoises and other scaly reptiles) have their testes inside the body near the loin, by the kidneys.
quote: this applies (among animals breathing air and having a lung) to all birds and oviparous quadrupeds. For all these have their testes internal near the loin
scope: Birds and oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, tortoises, crocodiles)
measurable_quantities: position of the testes (internal near the kidneys or external) in birds and reptiles
candidate_data: Comparative anatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; museum specimens in MorphoSource.

label: The uterus is always double
claim: The uterus is always double, just as the testes of the male are always two.
quote: The uterus is always double, just as the testes are always two in the male.
scope: All females with a uterus or its analogue, including crustaceans, cephalopods and larger insects
measurable_quantities: number of uterine horns or paired oviducts across taxa
candidate_data: Comparative reproductive anatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Animals with only ducts or internal testes copulate more quickly
claim: Animals that have no testes but only ducts, or that have internal testes, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation than animals with external testes.
quote: so those which have not testes but only ducts, or which have them indeed but internally, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation.
scope: Fishes, snakes, birds and oviparous quadrupeds compared with mammals with external testes
measurable_quantities: copulation duration
testis position (absent, internal, scrotal)
candidate_data: Published compilations of copulation duration across vertebrates, matched to testis position from Phenoscape.

label: Seasonally breeding birds' testes swell in the breeding season and shrink after
claim: Birds' testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and in birds that pair at one season of the year they become so small afterwards as to be almost indiscernible.
quote: for their testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and all those which pair at one season of the year have them so small when this is past that they are almost indiscernible
scope: Birds, especially seasonal breeders
measurable_quantities: testis mass in and out of the breeding season
candidate_data: Published avian gonad-mass measurements across the annual cycle; AVONET for species traits and breeding seasonality.

label: Hedgehogs copulate standing upright because of their spines
claim: Hedgehogs do not mount the female from behind like other quadrupeds but copulate standing upright, because of their spines.
quote: for the hedgehog does not, like the other quadrupeds, mount upon the back of the female, but they conjugate standing upright because of their spines.
scope: Hedgehog (Erinaceus)
measurable_quantities: copulatory posture of hedgehogs
candidate_data: Behavioural accounts of Erinaceus mating in the Animal Diversity Web and the primary literature.

label: Elephant and hedgehog have internal testes because their skin is unsuitable
claim: The testes are internal in the elephant and the hedgehog, because their skin is not suited to form a separate protective covering (scrotum) for them.
quote: For the same reason they are internal in the elephant and hedgehog, for the skin of these, too, is not well suited to keep the protective part separate.
scope: Elephants and hedgehogs, alongside cetaceans, birds and scaly reptiles
measurable_quantities: testis position in elephants and hedgehogs
candidate_data: Mammalian testicular-descent data compiled in comparative anatomy literature; Phenoscape and Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers bear live young from eggs formed inside
claim: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers first produce eggs internally and then bring forth their young alive.
quote: But the cartilaginous fish and the vipers produce their young alive externally, but first produce eggs internally.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes: sharks and rays) and vipers
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparous, ovoviviparous, viviparous) of sharks, rays and vipers
candidate_data: Reproductive-mode fields in FishBase and the Amniote Life-History Database / reptile databases.

label: Ovoviviparous animals keep their eggs inside because they are cold
claim: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers do not lay their eggs outside because they are of a cold nature, which leaves the egg-shell soft and unprotected.
quote: It is because they are of a cold nature, not hot as some assert, that they do not lay their eggs externally.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes) and vipers
measurable_quantities: body temperature or metabolic rate
egg-shell hardness
reproductive mode
candidate_data: FishBase and the Amniote Life-History Database for reproductive mode, with comparative metabolic-rate compilations.

label: Cephalopods copulate mouth to mouth with arms entwined
claim: Cephalopods copulate by entwining at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.
quote: The cephalopoda entwine together at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.
scope: Cephalopods: octopus, cuttlefish, squid
measurable_quantities: mating posture in cephalopod species
candidate_data: Cephalopod mating-behaviour literature and SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: The octopus arm inserted in the female's funnel is not a generative organ
claim: The arm that the male octopus inserts into the female's funnel serves only for attachment and is not an organ useful for generation, being outside the male's seminal passage.
quote: is only for the sake of attachment, and it is not an organ useful for generation, for it is outside the passage in the male and indeed outside the body of the male altogether.
scope: Octopus (poulp) and other cephalopods with a hectocotylus
measurable_quantities: sperm transfer by the hectocotylus arm
candidate_data: Cephalopod reproductive anatomy literature on the hectocotylus; SeaLifeBase species accounts.

label: Fleas, flies and cantharides arise from putrefying matter
claim: Some insects, such as fleas, flies and cantharides, do not come from parents but from putrefying matter, and although they unite and generate, they produce only a scolex (larva), not a creature of their own kind.
quote: these insects do not come into being from animals but from putrefying matter, liquid or solid; such are fleas, flies, and cantharides.
scope: Fleas, flies and blister beetles (cantharides); gnats and similar insects said to arise without any union
measurable_quantities: occurrence of insect emergence from decaying matter without eggs from parents
candidate_data: Life-cycle descriptions of Siphonaptera, Diptera and Meloidae in the Animal Diversity Web and entomological literature.

label: In most mating insects the female is larger than the male
claim: In most insects that copulate, the female is larger than the male.
quote: In most of those which unite the female is larger than the male.
scope: Insects that reproduce by copulation
measurable_quantities: female-to-male body size ratio across insect species
candidate_data: Published comparative datasets of insect sexual size dimorphism.

label: In most insects the female inserts a part into the male
claim: In most insects the male does not insert any part into the female; instead the female inserts a part of herself from below upwards into the male.
quote: In most cases the male does not insert any part into the female, but the female from below upwards into the male
scope: Insects that copulate
measurable_quantities: direction of genital insertion during insect copulation
candidate_data: Insect genital morphology and copulation studies; no compiled database known.

label: Resemblances to ancestors can skip generations
claim: Children may resemble remote ancestors from whom nothing has come to them, since resemblances recur after an interval of generations.
quote: Further, children are like their more remote ancestors from whom nothing has come, for the resemblances recur at an interval of many generations
scope: Humans, with the example of a woman of Elis and an Ethiopian
measurable_quantities: recurrence of grandparental traits absent in the parent generation
candidate_data: Human pedigree and heritability studies; Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) for recessive traits.

label: Semen does not come from all parts of the body
claim: Semen is not drawn from every part of the parent's body, contrary to those who explain inheritance that way.
quote: Into this we must next inquire, since it is plain that the semen is not secreted from all the parts.
scope: All animals that emit semen
measurable_quantities: origin of the germ line versus somatic tissues
candidate_data: none known

label: Mutilated parents do not always have mutilated young
claim: The young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as young are not always like their parents.
quote: And the young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as they are not always like their parents
scope: Animals and humans with acquired injuries
measurable_quantities: frequency of parental acquired injuries appearing in offspring
candidate_data: Experimental studies on non-inheritance of acquired mutilations; no compiled database known.

label: Large animals have few young, small animals many
claim: Large animals have few young and small animals have many.
quote: A further proof that it is not a waste-product, but rather a secretion, is the fact that the large animals have few young, the small many.
scope: Animals generally
measurable_quantities: adult body mass
litter or clutch size
annual fecundity
candidate_data: AnAge, PanTHERIA, the Amniote Life-History Database and FishBase for body mass and offspring number.

label: Humans gain half their adult height in about the first five years
claim: In human beings the body gains in about the first five years half the height that it gains in all the rest of life.
quote: for in about five years, in the case of human beings at any rate, the body seems to gain half the height that is gained in all the rest of life.
scope: Humans
measurable_quantities: height at age five as a fraction of adult height
candidate_data: WHO Child Growth Standards and national growth charts (e.g. CDC growth charts).

label: Fat people are less fertile because the secretion turns to fat
claim: Fat people, women as well as men, are less fertile than others, because in the well-nourished the secretion being concocted turns to fat instead of semen.
quote: And fat people, women as well as men, appear to be less fertile than others from the fact that the secretion when in process of concoction turns to fat with those who are too well-nourished.
scope: Humans; also fat he-goats and luxuriant vines
measurable_quantities: body mass index or adiposity
fertility or time to conception
candidate_data: Epidemiological cohort studies relating body mass index to fertility in men and women.

label: Semen is a secretion of useful nutriment in its last stage
claim: Semen is a secretion (residue) of useful nutriment in its final stage, not a waste-product of the body.
quote: From what has been said, it is clear that semen is a secretion of useful nutriment, and that in its last stage, whether it is produced by all or no.
scope: All animals that produce semen
candidate_data: none known

label: Semen and menstruation begin at the same age
claim: Semen begins to appear in males at the same time of life as the menstrual flow begins in females, together with the change of voice and the development of the breasts.
quote: For the semen begins to appear in males and to be emitted at the same time of life that the catamenia begin to flow in females
scope: Humans
measurable_quantities: age at spermarche
age at menarche
candidate_data: Population studies of pubertal timing reporting age at menarche and spermarche.

label: Among viviparous animals females are smaller because of menstruation
claim: Among the viviparous animals females are smaller than males, because the secretion that would build the body is discharged as menstrual fluid, and this is the only class that menstruates.
quote: the same cause accounts for the fact that the bulk of the body is smaller in females than in males among the vivipara, since this is the only class in which the catamenia are discharged from the body.
scope: Viviparous animals (mammals), especially humans
measurable_quantities: female-to-male body mass ratio in mammals
presence of menstruation
candidate_data: PanTHERIA and the Amniote Life-History Database for sex-specific body mass; literature on menstruating mammals.

label: The female is a kind of impotent male, unable to concoct semen
claim: The female is, as it were, an impotent male: she is female through an incapacity to concoct the final nutriment into semen.
quote: the woman is as it were an impotent male, for it is through a certain incapacity that the female is female, being incapable of concocting the nutriment in its last stage into semen
scope: Females of all animals with two sexes, especially women
candidate_data: none known

label: All directly viviparous animals menstruate, though less than women
claim: All animals that are viviparous without first producing eggs (man and the viviparous quadrupeds) have a menstrual discharge, unless defective like the mule, though the discharge is not as abundant as in women.
quote: all these have the catamenia, unless they are defective in development as the mule, only the efflux is not abundant as in women.
scope: Humans and viviparous quadrupeds (placental mammals); the mule as an exception
measurable_quantities: presence and volume of menstrual or oestrous bleeding across mammals
candidate_data: Comparative literature on menstruation and oestrous bleeding across mammals; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Menstruation usually begins when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth
claim: Menstruation generally begins in girls when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth.
quote: for it is when they have risen two fingers’ breadth that the catamenia generally begin.
scope: Human females at puberty
measurable_quantities: breast development stage at menarche
candidate_data: Pubertal-staging cohort studies relating Tanner breast stage to age at menarche.

label: Nothing material from the male need enter the embryo; he imparts motion and form
claim: Nothing material from the male needs to become part of the embryo; what comes from him acts only by imparting motion and form, as the medical art cures a patient.
quote: It is plain then that it is not necessary that anything at all should come away from the male, and if anything does come away it does not follow that this gives rise to the embryo as being in the embryo, but only as that which imparts the motion and as the form
scope: All animals with two sexes
measurable_quantities: material contribution of the sperm to the zygote
candidate_data: none known

label: A hen producing wind-eggs can be made fertile by treading while the egg is yellow
claim: If a hen producing wind-eggs is trodden by a cock before the egg has begun to whiten, while it is still all yolk, the eggs become fertile instead of wind-eggs.
quote: For if a hen-bird is in process of producing wind-eggs and is then trodden by the cock before the egg has begun to whiten and while it is all still yellow, then they become fertile instead of being wind-eggs.
scope: Domestic fowl and other birds that lay wind-eggs (unfertilized eggs)
measurable_quantities: fertility of eggs by timing of insemination relative to albumen deposition
candidate_data: Poultry science studies on the timing of fertilization relative to ovulation and albumen formation.

label: A hen trodden by a second cock while the egg is yellow bears chicks like the second
claim: If a hen is trodden by a second cock while her eggs are still yolk, the whole brood of chicks turns out like the second cock.
quote: And if while it is still yellow she be trodden by another cock, the whole brood of chicks turn out like the second cock.
scope: Domestic fowl
measurable_quantities: paternity of chicks after successive matings with two cocks
candidate_data: Poultry sperm-competition and last-male-precedence studies.

label: In oviparous fishes only the eggs reached by the milt are fertilized
claim: In oviparous fishes the male sprinkles milt over the eggs after they are laid, and only the eggs the milt reaches are fertilized.
quote: When the female has laid her eggs, the male spinkles the milt over them, and those eggs are fertilized which it reaches, but not the others
scope: Oviparous fishes with external fertilization
measurable_quantities: fertilization rate of eggs by milt contact
candidate_data: FishBase reproduction fields (fertilization mode) and aquaculture fertilization studies.

label: In all animals that move about the sexes are separate
claim: In all animals that can move about, the sexes are separate, one individual male and another female of the same species, whereas in plants they are combined.
quote: In all animals which can move about, the sexes are separated, one individual being male and one female, though both are the same in species, as with man and horse.
scope: Locomotory animals (contrasted with plants and sessile animals)
measurable_quantities: frequency of gonochorism versus hermaphroditism among motile animal taxa
candidate_data: Comparative datasets of animal sexual systems; Animal Diversity Web and Open Tree of Life for taxon coverage.

label: Generation makes kinds eternal as species, not as individuals
claim: Animals generate because a living thing cannot be eternal as an individual but can be eternal as a species, which is why there is always a race of men, animals and plants.
quote: Now it is impossible for it to be eternal as an individual (though of course the real essence of things is in the individual)— were it such it would be eternal — but it is possible for it as a species.
scope: All animals and plants
candidate_data: none known

label: Animals with blood are larger than bloodless ones, and mobile larger than fixed
claim: Taken generally, animals with blood are larger than bloodless animals, and animals that move about are larger than those that stay fixed.
quote: Therefore, taking a general view, we may say that sanguinea are of greater size than bloodless animals, and those which move about than those which remain fixed.
scope: Animals with blood (roughly vertebrates) versus bloodless animals (invertebrates); motile versus sessile animals
measurable_quantities: body size distributions of vertebrates versus invertebrates
body size of motile versus sessile taxa
candidate_data: Body-size compilations such as AnAge, PanTHERIA, FishBase and SeaLifeBase, with Open Tree of Life for taxonomy.

label: Eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods grow after being laid
claim: The eggs of birds and oviparous reptiles are complete when laid and do not grow, whereas the eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods are imperfect and increase in size after being laid.
quote: The eggs of others are imperfect; such are those of fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods, for their eggs increase after being produced.
scope: Fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods, contrasted with birds and oviparous reptiles
measurable_quantities: egg size at laying versus before hatching
candidate_data: Egg-size and development studies in fishes and invertebrates; FishBase and SeaLifeBase egg data.

label: All viviparous animals have blood
claim: All viviparous animals have blood, and animals with blood are either viviparous or oviparous unless altogether infertile.
quote: All the vivipara are sanguineous, and the sanguinea are either viviparous or oviparous, except those which are altogether infertile.
scope: Viviparous animals and animals with blood
measurable_quantities: occurrence of viviparity in invertebrate (bloodless) taxa
candidate_data: Reproductive-mode data for invertebrates in SeaLifeBase and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: Only air-breathing animals are internally viviparous
claim: No animal is internally viviparous unless it takes in and breathes out air.
quote: for nothing is internally viviparous unless it receive and breathe out air.
scope: Internally viviparous animals (man, viviparous quadrupeds, cetaceans)
measurable_quantities: occurrence of placental viviparity in water-breathing taxa
candidate_data: Reproductive-mode data in FishBase and the Amniote Life-History Database.

label: Animals with lungs are hotter than animals without
claim: Animals with a lung are generally hotter than those without, and among them those whose lung is soft and full of blood are hottest.
quote: for generally those animals which have a lung are hotter than those which have not
scope: Air-breathing animals compared with gill-breathers and others
measurable_quantities: body temperature or metabolic rate by respiratory organ
candidate_data: Comparative body-temperature and metabolic-rate compilations; AnAge records metabolic rate and temperature.

label: Heat and dryness explain why birds and reptiles lay complete eggs
claim: Birds and scaly reptiles lay a complete egg because they are hot, but only an egg rather than live young because they are dry; the reproductive mode follows from an animal's heat and moisture.
quote: For birds and scaly reptiles because of their heat produce a perfect egg, but because of their dryness it is only an egg
scope: Birds and scaly reptiles, within his heat-and-moisture account of viviparity and oviparity
measurable_quantities: body temperature
body water content
reproductive mode
candidate_data: Amniote Life-History Database for reproductive mode with comparative body-temperature data.

label: All insects produce a scolex and all insects are bloodless
claim: All insects produce a scolex (larva), all insects are bloodless, and so every animal that produces a scolex is bloodless.
quote: All insects produce a scolex. Now all the insects are bloodless, wherefore all creatures that produce a scolex from themselves are so.
scope: Insects
measurable_quantities: occurrence of a larval stage across insect orders
candidate_data: Life-cycle data for insect orders in the Animal Diversity Web and entomological literature.

label: Nature orders generation in a graded series by heat and perfection
claim: Nature orders generation in a regular gradation: the hottest and most perfect animals bear live young internally, then come those viviparous after internal eggs, then those laying perfect eggs, then those laying imperfect eggs, and coldest of all those producing a scolex.
quote: We must observe how rightly Nature orders generation in regular gradation. The more perfect and hotter animals produce their young perfect in respect of quality
scope: All animals, from mammals to insects
measurable_quantities: metabolic rate or body temperature against reproductive mode
candidate_data: Amniote Life-History Database and AnAge for reproductive mode and metabolic data.

label: Embryonic parts form in succession, not all together
claim: The parts of an embryo do not all exist from the start; some are visible in the embryo while others are not yet formed, so they come into being in succession.
quote: That the former is not the fact is plain even to the senses, for some of the parts are clearly visible as already existing in the embryo while others are not
scope: Animal embryos
measurable_quantities: timing of organ appearance in embryonic development
candidate_data: Developmental staging series and anatomy ontologies with stage annotations (e.g. Uberon, Bgee).

label: The lung appears later than the heart in development though larger
claim: In development the lung appears later than the heart, even though it is larger, so late appearance is not due to small size.
quote: for the lung is of greater size than the heart, and yet appears later than the heart in the original development.
scope: Animals with heart and lungs
measurable_quantities: embryonic stage of first appearance of heart and lung
candidate_data: Embryonic staging data in Uberon and Bgee developmental annotations.

label: General animal characters develop before those of the species
claim: An embryo does not become an animal and a particular kind of animal at the same time; the characters peculiar to the species develop last.
quote: For e.g. an animal does not become at the same time an animal and a man or a horse or any other particular animal. For the end is developed last, and the peculiar character of the species is the end of the generation in each individual.
scope: Animal embryos
measurable_quantities: developmental timing of general versus species-specific traits
candidate_data: Comparative embryology and gene-expression time series across species (e.g. Bgee).

label: Reason alone enters from outside and is divine
claim: Of the kinds of soul, reason alone enters the embryo from outside and alone is divine, since its activity has no connection with any bodily activity.
quote: It remains, then, for the reason alone so to enter and alone to be divine, for no bodily activity has any connexion with the activity of reason.
scope: Animals that have reason (humans)
candidate_data: none known

label: Semen is thick and white when emitted and becomes watery on cooling
claim: Semen is thick and white when it issues from the body but on cooling becomes liquid and colourless like water, and in frost it liquefies rather than freezing.
quote: For whereas when it issues from the animal it is thick and white, yet on cooling it becomes liquid as water, and its colour is that of water.
scope: Semen of animals, chiefly human
measurable_quantities: semen viscosity over time after ejaculation
semen colour
candidate_data: Clinical semen-analysis literature on coagulation and liquefaction (e.g. WHO laboratory manual reference values).

label: Semen is always white, including that of Ethiopians
claim: Semen is invariably white, so Herodotus was wrong that the semen of Ethiopians is black.
quote: for it is also an invariable rule that it is white, and Herodotus does not report the truth when he says that the semen of the Aethiopians is black
scope: Humans of all populations, and animals generally
measurable_quantities: semen colour across human populations
candidate_data: Clinical semen-analysis literature.

label: Some cartilaginous fishes complete development by connection to the uterus
claim: In some cartilaginous fishes, once the nutriment of the egg is used up, the embryo completes its development by connection with the uterus, so the egg is not released from the uterus.
quote: in other cases, when the nutriment from the egg is consumed, development is completed by connection with the uterus, and therefore the egg is not set free from the uterus.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes), e.g. placental sharks such as the smooth dogfish
measurable_quantities: presence of a yolk-sac placenta in shark species
candidate_data: FishBase reproductive-mode fields and the elasmobranch reproduction literature.

label: Menstruation tends to come during the waning of the moon
claim: The menstrual period in women is not exactly fixed but tends to come during the waning of the moon, because bodies are colder when the environment is colder.
quote: The period is not accurately defined in women, but tends to return during the waning of the moon.
scope: Women
measurable_quantities: menstrual onset dates relative to lunar phase
candidate_data: Large menstrual-cycle tracking datasets and published studies of menstruation and lunar phase.

label: Hybrids come to resemble the female line over successive generations
claim: When different kinds are crossed, the first cross resembles both parents, but over successive generations the offspring come to resemble the female in form.
quote: the first cross has a common resemblance to both parents, as the hybrid between fox and dog, partridge and domestic fowl, but as time goes on and one generation springs from another, the final result resembles the female in form
scope: Crosses between related kinds (fox and dog, partridge and fowl), possible when gestation, breeding season and size are similar
measurable_quantities: phenotypic resemblance of backcross generations to maternal versus paternal species
candidate_data: Hybridization and introgression studies in birds and canids; no compiled database known.

label: The heart is the first part to be distinctly formed in all animals with blood
claim: In all animals with blood the heart is the first part to appear distinctly formed in the embryo, being the origin of the blood-vessels and of the other parts.
quote: Therefore it is that the heart appears first distinctly marked off in all the sanguinea
scope: Animals with blood (roughly vertebrates); the heart's analogue in bloodless animals
measurable_quantities: order of organ differentiation in vertebrate embryos
candidate_data: Vertebrate embryonic staging series with stage-annotated anatomy in Uberon and Bgee.

label: No male of the erythrinus has ever been seen
claim: No male of the fish called erythrinus has ever been seen, only females and specimens full of roe, which suggests it may generate without a male.
quote: No male of the so-called erythrinus has ever yet been seen, but females, and specimens full of roe, have been seen.
scope: The erythrinus (a Mediterranean fish, probably a sea bass or sea bream of the Serranidae or Sparidae)
measurable_quantities: sex ratio and sexual system of the species
candidate_data: FishBase reproduction fields on hermaphroditism in Serranus and related fishes.

label: Eels and some mullets are neither male nor female
claim: Some fishes are neither male nor female, such as eels and a kind of mullet found in stagnant waters.
quote: Again, some members of the class of fishes are neither male nor female, as eels and a kind of mullets found in stagnant waters.
scope: Eels (Anguilla) and a mullet of stagnant waters
measurable_quantities: presence of differentiated gonads in eels and mullets
candidate_data: FishBase species accounts and eel reproductive biology literature.

label: Nature makes nothing in vain, so the male is needed for full generation
claim: Where the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly alone, for otherwise the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.
quote: But whenever the sexes are separate the female cannot generate perfectly by herself alone, for then the male would exist in vain, and Nature makes nothing in vain.
scope: All animals with separate sexes
candidate_data: none known

label: Internal parts form before external parts in the embryo
claim: In the embryo the internal parts come into being before the external, and the larger become visible before the smaller.
quote: After this, as said already, the internal parts come into being before the external.
scope: Animal embryos
measurable_quantities: developmental stage of first appearance of internal versus external structures
candidate_data: Embryonic staging series with stage-annotated anatomy in Uberon and Bgee.

label: Polydactylous quadrupeds bear blind young whose eyelids open after birth
claim: All polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds, such as the dog, lion, wolf, fox and jackal, bear their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate until after birth.
quote: Moreover, all polydactylous quadrupeds, as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal, produce their young blind, and the eyelids do not separate till after birth.
scope: Polydactylous (many-toed) quadrupeds: carnivores such as dog, lion, wolf, fox, jackal
measurable_quantities: eyes closed or open at birth
age at eye opening
candidate_data: AnAge and the Amniote Life-History Database for neonatal development; Animal Diversity Web species accounts on altricial young.

label: In the early embryo the head and eyes are largest and the legs small
claim: In the embryo at an early stage the parts about the head, especially the eyes, appear largest and the parts below the navel, such as the legs, are small, because the lower parts exist for the sake of the upper.
quote: This is why the parts about the head, and particularly the eyes, appear largest in the embryo at an early stage, while the parts below the umbilicus, as the legs, are small
scope: Animal embryos with an upper and lower body
measurable_quantities: relative size of head, eyes and limbs across embryonic stages
candidate_data: Embryo morphometric data from staging series and specimens in MorphoSource.

label: Eyes appear very large early but are the last parts to be completed
claim: The eyes of all animals, whether walking, swimming or flying, appear very large from the beginning of development but are the last parts to be completely formed, collapsing in the interval.
quote: Though from the beginning they appear very large in all creatures, whether they walk or swim or fly, yet they are the last of the parts to be formed completely, for in the intervening time they collapse.
scope: Embryos of vertebrates
measurable_quantities: relative eye size and stage of eye completion in embryos
candidate_data: Embryonic staging series with stage-annotated anatomy in Uberon and Bgee.

label: The bregma is the last bone to form and is still soft after birth
claim: The bregma (the top of the skull) is the last bone to be formed and is still soft in children after birth, more so in man than in other animals because man's brain is the most fluid and largest.
quote: For this reason the ‘bregma’ is the last of the bones to be formed; even after birth this bone is still soft in children.
scope: Humans, compared with other animals with a brain
measurable_quantities: age at closure of the anterior fontanelle
order of ossification of skull bones
candidate_data: Paediatric data on anterior fontanelle closure and comparative cranial ossification sequences.

label: Bones set the limit of an animal's size
claim: Bones grow only up to a certain point, and they set the limit of size in animals; if bones could always grow, every animal with bone or its analogue would grow as long as it lived.
quote: if these had been always able to grow, all animals that have bone or its analogue would grow as long as they lived, for these set the limit of size to animals.
scope: Animals with bone or its analogue
measurable_quantities: growth patterns (determinate or indeterminate) across vertebrates
candidate_data: Growth-pattern data in AnAge and FishBase (e.g. lifelong growth in fishes and reptiles).

label: Hair goes on growing after death
claim: Hair continues to grow after death, though it does not begin growing then.
quote: Hair actually goes on growing after death; it does not, however, begin growing then.
scope: Humans and hairy animals
measurable_quantities: hair shaft length change after death
candidate_data: Forensic and post-mortem studies of hair and nail length.

label: Of all bones only the teeth grow throughout life
claim: Of all the bones, the teeth alone go on growing throughout life, as shown by teeth that grow out of line until they no longer meet.
quote: Of all the bones they alone go on growing through life, as is plain with the teeth which grow out of the straight line so as no longer to touch each other.
scope: Animals with bones and teeth
measurable_quantities: presence of continuously growing (hypselodont) teeth across mammals
candidate_data: Dental morphology data in Phenoscape and MorphoSource; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Other animals are born with teeth but man is born without
claim: Other animals are born with teeth or their analogue, because they are more perfect at birth than man, whereas man is normally born without teeth.
quote: Other animals are born in possession of teeth or their analogue (unless in cases contrary to Nature), because when they are set free from the parent they are more perfect than man; but man (also unless in cases contrary to Nature) is born without them.
scope: Humans compared with other toothed animals
measurable_quantities: presence of erupted teeth at birth across mammals
candidate_data: Neonatal dentition data in the Animal Diversity Web and the comparative dental literature.

label: Man is the most naked animal and has the smallest nails for his size
claim: Man is the most naked of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size, because he has the least earthy residue.
quote: man is the most naked in body of all animals and has the smallest nails in proportion to his size
scope: Humans compared with other animals
measurable_quantities: body hair density across mammals
nail or claw size relative to body size
candidate_data: Comparative mammalian hair-density studies and morphology specimens in MorphoSource.

label: Umbilical cord vessel number rises with animal size
claim: The umbilical cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath: more numerous in larger animals such as cattle, one in the smallest animals, and two in those of intermediate size.
quote: The cord consists of blood-vessels in a sheath, more numerous in the larger animals as cattle and the like, one in the smallest, two in those of intermediate size.
scope: Viviparous animals with an umbilical cord (placental mammals)
measurable_quantities: number of umbilical vessels
adult body mass
candidate_data: Comparative placentation and umbilical cord anatomy literature; PanTHERIA for body mass.

label: Animals lacking upper front teeth have cotyledons in the uterus
claim: All animals without front teeth in the upper jaw, and those with front teeth in both jaws whose uterus has many close blood-vessels rather than one great one, have cotyledons in the uterus; most with front teeth in both jaws and no horns lack them.
quote: All animals with no front teeth in the upper jaw, and all those which have them in both jaws and whose uterus has not one great blood-vessel running through it but many close together insteadall these have in the uterus the so-called cotyledons
scope: Viviparous quadrupeds; animals without upper incisors (ruminants) versus those with incisors in both jaws
measurable_quantities: presence of upper incisors
placenta type (cotyledonary or not)
candidate_data: Comparative placentation literature matched to dental characters in Phenoscape; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: Cotyledons shrink and disappear as the embryo matures
claim: As the embryo grows and approaches completion, the cotyledons in the uterus become smaller and finally disappear when it is fully formed.
quote: As the embryo grows and approaches perfection the cotyledons become smaller and finally disappear when it is perfected.
scope: Animals with cotyledons in the uterus (ruminants)
measurable_quantities: cotyledon size across gestation
candidate_data: Veterinary placentome morphometry studies in cattle and sheep.

label: Of all hybrids only mules are sterile
claim: Animals born of crosses between different kinds can all mate and produce young of both sexes, except mules, which alone are sterile.
quote: Of the animals that arise from such union all except mules are found to copulate again with each other and to be able to produce young of both sexes, but mules alone are sterile
scope: Hybrids between related kinds (dogs, foxes, wolves, partridges and hens, hawks, rays), contrasted with mules
measurable_quantities: fertility of interspecific hybrids
candidate_data: Published compilations of hybrid fertility in mammals and birds.

label: General theories not based on the special principles of a subject are empty
claim: All theories not based on the special principles of the subject in question are empty: in natural science one must reason from the facts peculiar to the kinds concerned, as geometry reasons from geometrical principles.
quote: For all theories not based on the special principles involved are empty; they only appear to be connected with the facts without being so really.
scope: Method of natural science
candidate_data: none known

label: The gestation period of both horse and ass is one year
claim: The period of gestation in both the horse and the ass is one year, so the mother gives birth in the same season as she was impregnated.
quote: for the mothers bear at the same season as that in which they are impregnated, the period of gestation in both horse and ass being one year.
scope: Horse (Equus caballus) and ass (Equus asinus)
measurable_quantities: gestation length in horses and donkeys
candidate_data: AnAge and PanTHERIA gestation-length records.

label: The ass cannot bear cold and is not found in cold regions
claim: The ass is of a cold nature and cannot bear cold, so it is not produced in wintry regions such as Scythia and the land of the Celts beyond Iberia.
quote: Again the ass is an animal of cold nature, and so is not wont to be produced in wintry regions because it cannot bear cold, as in Scythia and the neighbouring country and among the Celts beyond Iberia
scope: Domestic ass (Equus asinus)
measurable_quantities: historical and present distribution of donkeys by climate
candidate_data: GBIF occurrence records and FAO livestock statistics for donkey distribution against climate.

label: The mule is sterile because the ass's cold seed chills the horse's
claim: Mules are sterile because the horse already tends to sterility and becomes wholly so when its generative secretion is chilled by mixing with the cold secretion of the ass.
quote: The horse is much the same; it tends naturally towards sterility, and to make it entirely so it is only necessary that its generative secretion should become colder; now this is what happens to it when mixed with the corresponding secretion of the ass.
scope: Mule (horse × ass hybrid)
measurable_quantities: semen temperature or quality in horses and asses
fertility of mules
candidate_data: Equine reproductive and cytogenetic studies of mule sterility.

label: A female mule can conceive but cannot carry the foal to birth
claim: A female mule can sometimes conceive, but she cannot nourish the embryo to birth because she has no menstrual secretion.
quote: Hence it is sometimes possible for the female to conceive, as has been known to happen before now, but it is impossible for her to complete the process of nourishing the embryo and bringing it to birth.
scope: Female mules
measurable_quantities: documented pregnancies and live births in female mules
candidate_data: Veterinary case reports of mule pregnancies and foalings.
